recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No further core FHIR source work is needed for FHIR-38654; any remaining XHTML-id handling belongs in tooling rather than in Questionnaire.item.linkId's datatype or guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-38654 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core technical correction asking whether Questionnaire.item.linkId should prohibit spaces after Publisher-generated XHTML narrative used linkIds directly as element IDs and produced invalid XHTML. The final resolution was that linkIds can have whitespace and slashes by design, and tooling should not rely on linkIds being valid XHTML element IDs or embed them directly as such.
initial_application: The Jira application comment identifies git commit d3cf3998e5a1db5f7faaa013f182d47543decdfc, 'FHIR-38654 - Added guidance on linkId.' The commit diff is noisy from line-ending churn, but the intended guidance is present in the current Questionnaire.item.linkId comment.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists questionnaire as an active resource, so source/questionnaire/structuredefinition-Questionnaire.xml is in build scope. FHIR-I WGM 2022 minutes referencing FHIR-38654 record that Element.id was a red herring, linkId was intended to allow whitespace and slashes, and tooling should handle them. The triggering FHIR-38642 IG issue remains Triaged and is not a final core source decision. Later Applied issue FHIR-46191 added regex constraints for leading/trailing and non-single-space intervening whitespace while preserving linkId as string and preserving slash use; FHIR-46191 is already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current Questionnaire.item.linkId source remains string, says linkIds can have whitespaces and slashes by design, and says tooling should not treat linkIds as valid XHTML element IDs. The later regex constraint narrows whitespace shape but does not reverse the FHIR-38654 guidance.
